# Overriding a node's state through the debug channel

`POST /v1/instances/{id}/debug/override` sets an attribute or invalidates a node
on a live instance. It is open in exactly two states — the instance is paused,
or it sits at an unresumed pause-mode breakpoint hit — and shut on either side
of them.

## The template

A counter, a knob node to invalidate, and a worker that parks against a
rate-limited endpoint so the frame stays open while you work.

```yaml
name: debug-channel-demo
version: "1"
nodes:
  - type: emitter
    kind: loop_counter
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          max: {type: integer, default: 9}
          count: {type: integer}

  - type: knob
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: emitter
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          tick: {type: integer, default: 7}

  - type: worker
    executor: http-node
    subscribes:
      - node: emitter
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
      - node: emitter
        type: attribute/count/changed
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          url:    {type: string, default: "http://endpoint:8000/work"}
          method: {type: string, default: POST}
          seen:   {type: integer, source: "{{nodes.emitter.attribute.count}}"}
```

## The channel is shut by default

With the instance running and the worker parked, and no breakpoint installed:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/debug/override" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"action":"invalidate_node","node_type":"knob"}'
# 409 instance not in debuggable state, states: ["breakpoint","paused"]
```

The same 409 answers a `set_attribute` override. Reading the node back afterwards
shows its attribute values untouched — the refusal changed nothing.

## Pausing opens it

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/pause" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}'

curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/debug/override" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"action":"set_attribute","node_type":"worker",
       "attribute_key":"injected","attribute_value":"set-by-operator"}'
# 200 {"gate_state":"paused","runs_mutated":1}

curl -sS "$BASE/v1/nodes/$WORKER_NODE_ID"
# latest_attributes now carries injected: set-by-operator
```

Invalidating a node answers on the same open channel:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/debug/override" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"action":"invalidate_node","node_type":"knob"}'
# 200 {"gate_state":"paused","runs_mutated":1}
```

No work runs while the instance stays paused. Resume it and the consequences
play out:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/resume" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}'
```

The invalidated node dispatches again. The operator inspects and mutates while
everything is still, then lets it run.

## A breakpoint hit opens it too

Install a pause-mode pre-dispatch breakpoint on the worker and let it hit,
without pausing the instance:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/breakpoints" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"matcher":{"node_type":"worker"},"checkpoint":"before_dispatch",
       "mode":"pause","hit_ttl_seconds":3600}'
```

At the unresumed hit, both override actions answer 200 with
`gate_state: breakpoint`, the overridden value reads back off the node, and the
invalidated node runs again once the hit is released.

## The channel shuts behind the session

Release the hit, delete the breakpoint, and let the instance settle. The same
override answers 409 again, naming the same two states.
